svg.title: Define the Buyer by the Pain You Fix
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-problem-led-buyer-definition; chapter number: 1; chart type: process_flow; title: Define the Buyer by the Pain You Fix; subtitle: From problem statement to a time-boxed pilot; caption: Targeting is built from problems and outcomes, then cut until only accounts with active, budgeted, urgent pain remain.; assumptions note: Steps combine separately reported practices from OGONJO Workbooks, Dan Martell, Hunter and Connor Murray; figures are attributed practitioner claims, not a single measured cohort.; note: Sources - OGONJO Workbooks (ZSqgCrydlAo, 4S63IHiDhTk), Dan Martell, Hunter (35H3HVb8ymw), Connor Murray (DBGq--oFsQ8).; stages: step: 01; label: Problem-Led ICP; value: Step 1; detail: Define the buyer by the pain, then run the Five Whys until the emotional reason to act surfaces. One SaaS redefined its ICP and reported +32% conversion and a 20% shorter sales cycle (OGONJO Workbooks).; step: 02; label: Scorecard Cut; value: Step 2; detail: Score 5 to 7 criteria against open deals and disqualify 20 to 30%; a strong ICP shows roughly a 3x win-rate gap between high and low scores (OGONJO Workbooks).; step: 03; label: Technographic Trim; value: Step 3; detail: Trim the universe with technographics, as Dan Martell cut 50,000 accounts to 800.; step: 04; label: Small-List Segments; value: Step 4; detail: Lists of 100 or fewer more than double replies; split a 10,000-lead list into 10 x 1,000 segments, keep each sending box at 50 or fewer per day, and email more than one person per company for almost +50% replies (Hunter).; step: 05; label: Time-Boxed Pilot; value: Step 5; detail: Before any POV, pilot or trial, agree use cases, requirements, people, timeline and success KPIs, and time-box it at 2 or 4 weeks (Connor Murray).
